issue.title: When using --experimental_remote_spawn_cache, runfiles are not restored correctly

repository.name: bazel
repository.description: a fast, scalable, multi-language and extensible build system

issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request / question:

If you do a `bazel build` or `bazel run` with `--experimental_remote_spawn_cache`, and if a built tool was restored from the remote cache rather than actually being built locally, then its runfiles are not restored properly, so the tool doesn't work.

For example, if you have an `sh_binary(name = "foo", srcs = ["foo.sh"])`, then the first time you do

    bazel run --experimental_remote_spawn_cache --remote_rest_cache=... :foo

it will work; but then if you `bazel clean` and then run the above command again, it will fail.

### If possible, provide a minimal example to reproduce the problem:

Make an empty `WORKSPACE` file. Put the following shell script in the same directory, and make it executable. This is a complete test to reproduce the above.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

# adjust these as appropriate for your env:
BAZEL=./bazel
REMOTE_REST_CACHE=http://localhost:12502

# Each time we run this test, we want to start clean, with nothing coming
# from the remote cache. So we pick a pseudorandom number, and we put it
# in the name of the shell script that we create.
random=$RANDOM$RANDOM

# create a simple shell script, mytool_$random.sh
cat > mytool_$random.sh <<EOF
#!/bin/bash
echo this is mytool
EOF
chmod +x mytool_$random.sh

# create a BUILD file with an sh_binary rule for that shell script
cat > BUILD <<EOF
sh_binary(
    name = "mytool_$random",
    srcs = ["mytool_$random.sh"],
)
EOF

echo "============ first 'bazel run' (nothing will come from the remote cache)"
(
    set -o xtrace
    $BAZEL clean >& /dev/null
    $BAZEL run --experimental_remote_spawn_cache --remote_rest_cache=$REMOTE_REST_CACHE :mytool_$random
)

echo
echo "============ second 'bazel run' (build artifacts will be downloaded from the remote cache)"
(
    set -o xtrace
    $BAZEL clean >& /dev/null
    $BAZEL run --experimental_remote_spawn_cache --remote_rest_cache=$REMOTE_REST_CACHE :mytool_$random
)
```

Output of the second 'bazel run' above:

```
ERROR: Error running program: java.io.IOException: Cannot run program "/home/vagrant/.cache/bazel/_bazel_vagrant/4fff92efcdd7651a3d49858fef7486b8/execroot/__main__/_bin/process-wrapper" (in directory "/home/vagrant/.cache/bazel/_bazel_vagrant/4fff92efcdd7651a3d49858fef7486b8/execroot/__main__/bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/bin/mytool_28279742.runfiles/__main__"): error=2, No such file or directory
```

### Environment info
* Operating System: macOS Sierra and Linux
* Bazel version (output of `bazel info release`): 0.8.1

body: For others who are tracking this, it looks like the above-mentioned commits (well, cherry-picks of them) are in the `release-0.9.0` branch, so I guess 0.9.0 will have this fix.
